title: Scottsdale Reconstruction & Rebuild Contractor | Gold Water Fire | Phoenix, AZ
description: Reconstruction and rebuild after fire or water damage in Scottsdale, AZ. Gold Water Fire rebuilds drywall, cabinetry, flooring and finishes. Call (480) 999-3339.
intro: The water is gone, the fans have been picked up, and now you are standing in a house with the drywall cut out at knee height and half your kitchen stacked in the garage. That gap between "the emergency is over" and "my home is back" is the part nobody warns you about, and it is where most people start carrying it alone: chasing an adjuster, pricing cabinets on a phone at midnight, trying to figure out whether the flooring you loved is even made anymore. If you have been holding all of that yourself for a few weeks now, you are not behind. You are at the point where this stops being one person's job.

sections.heading: Putting the house back, not just patching it
sections.body: Reconstruction is the phase after mitigation. Mitigation removes the water, the burned material, the soot, and the affected building materials. Reconstruction rebuilds what was removed and makes the finished result match the rest of your home. At Gold Water Fire, that work is led by Brandon Gurr, our Construction Manager, with Johnny as our Reconstruction Team Lead. Brandon came to us from Gurr Brothers Construction, so the rebuild side of this company is run by someone whose background is building, not just drying. That matters in Scottsdale, where the finish level in a lot of homes is the whole reason the house is worth what it is worth.

cards.heading: Structure and framing
cards.body: Replacing framing, subfloor and sheathing that had to come out, plus the sequencing behind it: insulation, vapor considerations, and getting the substrate flat and dry before anything decorative goes back on.

cards.heading: Drywall and finish work
cards.body: Hanging, taping, and matching existing texture. Knockdown and orange peel textures are common across Valley homes, and a patch that is technically fine but textured wrong is visible from across the room in Arizona light.

cards.heading: Kitchens, baths and cabinetry
cards.body: Cabinet boxes, countertops, tile, and plumbing fixture reset. Under-sink and dishwasher supply failures are one of the most common ways a kitchen ends up in reconstruction, and the damage usually runs into the adjacent flooring.

cards.heading: Flooring, paint and trim
cards.body: Tile, wood, LVP and carpet, with attention to where a new run meets an old one. Where an exact match is discontinued, we talk through transition options with you before anything is ordered.

sections.heading: Why Scottsdale rebuilds are their own kind of project
sections.body: Scottsdale is not one housing stock, it is several, and the rebuild changes with each. South Scottsdale near Osborn and Thomas has a dense band of 1950s and 1960s ranch homes, many built on slab with original galvanized or early copper supply lines and cast iron drains. When those fail, the leak often runs under the slab or inside a wall for a long time before anyone sees it, and the reconstruction ends up larger than the visible stain suggested. Central Scottsdale and the McCormick Ranch and Scottsdale Ranch areas are heavy with late 1970s and 1980s construction, which brings polybutylene-era plumbing concerns, flat and low-slope roof sections, and popcorn or heavy-texture ceilings that are hard to match without care. North Scottsdale, DC Ranch, Grayhawk, Troon and the McDowell Mountain foothills skews newer and larger: two-story great rooms, custom millwork, stone and specialty tile, tankless and multi-zone systems, and second-floor laundry rooms sitting directly above finished ceilings. Add HOA and design-review requirements common in those communities, plus City of Scottsdale permitting on structural and system work, and the paperwork is a real part of the timeline, not an afterthought.

cards.heading: Monsoon season, July into September
cards.body: Scottsdale sits where the McDowell Mountains and the desert wash system push runoff fast. Blowing rain drives water in through roof penetrations, parapet walls and flat-roof scuppers, then it shows up as a ceiling stain two rooms away from the actual entry point. Finding the real entry point is part of the rebuild scope.

cards.heading: Winter snowbird vacancies
cards.body: A lot of Scottsdale homes sit empty for months. A supply line that lets go in an unoccupied house runs until someone notices, so the reconstruction is usually whole-room or whole-floor rather than a spot repair, and secondary microbial growth becomes part of the conversation.

cards.heading: Summer heat and outdoor cooking
cards.body: Long stretches above 110 degrees stress water heaters, washing machine hoses and AC condensate lines, especially units in hot attics. On the fire side, built-in outdoor kitchens, fire features and dry desert landscaping close to the structure are a real ignition path in May and June before the rains come.

cards.heading: High-finish matching
cards.body: Stone slabs, specialty plaster, custom stain-grade cabinetry and imported tile are common here and are often no longer available in the same lot or run. Sourcing and honest conversations about substitution belong at the start of the project, not after demolition.

sections.heading: What the process actually looks like from here
sections.body: Reconstruction generally runs in a predictable order, and knowing the order is what makes a long project bearable. First a full walk of the loss with photos and measurements, so the scope reflects what is actually there rather than what the first inspection guessed. Then a written scope that lines up line by line with the way an insurance estimate is organized, which is what keeps supplements from turning into arguments later. Then permitting where the work requires it, then rough trades: framing, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, inspection. Then insulation and drywall, then paint, then finishes and cabinetry, then fixtures, then a punch walk where you point at anything that is not right. If mitigation is still in progress or has not started, our water damage restoration and fire damage restoration teams handle that phase, which means one company carries the file from the wet floor to the final coat of paint and nobody hands you off in the middle. You can read more about how we scope rebuild work on our reconstruction and rebuild page.

sections.heading: The part where you hand it over
sections.body: You have already done the hard, unglamorous work: you shut the water off, you made the call, you kept the family fed while the house was torn open. Handing the rebuild to someone else is not giving up on it, it is the point where the job needs a crew, a schedule and someone whose full-time work is talking to adjusters. Kristine handles the office side, Brooke coordinates water and mitigation scheduling, and Brandon and Johnny run the build. Jim Bennett and Jake Taylor founded Gold Water Fire, and we work under AZ ROC license #264344 (KB-2). We cover the full Phoenix metro area, from northwest Peoria to southeast Avondale, southwest San Tan Valley, northwest Apache Junction, and areas beyond that, so Scottsdale addresses from the Arcadia line up through Troon are squarely in our range. When you are ready, one phone call moves the whole thing off your plate: (480) 999-3339, or Help@goldwaterfire.com. More about the people doing the work is on our about page.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rebuild after water or fire damage in Scottsdale?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope. Cosmetic replacement of drywall, paint and flooring usually does not require a permit, while structural framing changes, panel or circuit work, gas line work, and mechanical replacements generally do. The City of Scottsdale handles permitting and inspection for work inside city limits, and many north Scottsdale communities add an HOA architectural or design review on anything visible from the exterior. We identify what applies to your address before demolition so it does not stall the schedule later.

faqs.q: My insurance estimate does not cover matching the rest of my flooring. What now?
faqs.a: This comes up constantly, especially with discontinued tile and wood species. Policies differ on whether they pay to continue a repair into an undamaged adjoining area for the sake of appearance. The practical path is to document the affected and adjoining areas carefully, get the actual availability of the original material in writing, and present that to the adjuster as part of the scope rather than as a change order after the fact. We will walk you through the options, including using a natural break or transition point, before anything gets ordered.

faqs.q: Can you handle both the cleanup and the rebuild, or do I need two companies?
faqs.a: Both. Gold Water Fire does water damage restoration, fire damage restoration, and reconstruction and rebuild. Keeping mitigation and reconstruction under one company means the crew that opened the wall is the same file as the crew that closes it, so the drying documentation, the scope and the final finish all line up instead of getting re-argued at the handoff.

faqs.q: Why is monsoon damage often bigger than it looks in Scottsdale homes?
faqs.a: Because of how water travels. Wind-driven rain enters at a roof penetration, parapet, scupper or a flat-roof seam, then runs along the top of a ceiling or down inside a wall cavity before it appears as a stain. The visible spot is often several feet from the entry point. On low-slope and flat roof sections, which are common in central Scottsdale, water can pool and soak insulation and sheathing before anything shows inside at all, so a proper rebuild starts with finding the actual entry path.

cta.heading: Let us take the rebuild from here
cta.body: Call (480) 999-3339 or email Help@goldwaterfire.com and tell us what happened and where in Scottsdale you are. We will come look at the house, write a scope you can actually read, and start putting it back. You have carried this long enough on your own.
